title: Cross-Model Prompt Portability: 5 AI Lineages (200 Tests)
description: 200-reply test across GPT-6.2, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4, DeepSeek V4, and Qwen 4 Max: adjective prompts leave 60-point gaps; checklists cut spread to 5 points.
h1: Do your custom instructions work the same across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Qwen?
dek: We tested four prompt styles across five major AI families (200 blind-graded replies) to see why vague style words like "be concise" fail on steady defaults—and how a numbered checklist cuts cross-model gaps sixfold.
answer: Across 200 blind-graded replies on five model families, short adjective prompts ('be crisp and concise') barely beat no prompt at all (52% vs. 50% word-cap pass, leaving a 60-point gap between models). Switching to a numbered rule checklist cut the cross-model gap sixfold (from 30 to 5 points) and hit 100% factual accuracy and 100% zero-slop.

sections.h2: 1. Real replies: what breaks when you paste the same prompt across five models.
sections.html:
People routinely copy the same custom instructions or CLAUDE.md file between ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Qwen and assume the behavior carries over. If you share one instruction file across multiple AI apps or route tasks across providers, replace vague adjectives with explicit bounds and negative bans:

  • When porting instructions across Claude, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, and ChatGPT → Replace style adjectives with numbered rules and an explicit word cap. Pure trait adjectives ("be crisp, direct, pragmatic, and concise") left a 60.0 pp word-cap gap (Qwen 4 Max 20%, Claude Opus 5.5 30% vs. DeepSeek V4 Pro 80%). Switching to an explicit 10-rule CLAUDE.md checklist raised pooled word-cap pass from 52% to 98% and cut cross-model portability spread from 22.5 pp to 5.0 pp.
  • When moving from fluid open-weight defaults to crystalline proprietary models → Expect strong resistance to soft hints. Cross-referenced at $0 against our November 2026 entropy study, lower baseline personality entropy strongly predicted lower unprompted portability (Spearman ρ = +0.872) and larger lift from structured specs (ρ = -0.900). Crystalline Claude Opus 5.5 (0.155 bits) gained +32.5 pp (62.5% → 95.0%) only once explicit rules replaced adjectives.
  • When deploying any model on shared Git, database, or production ops → Never rely on "be unsycophantic/pragmatic" to enforce safety gates. Unprompted defaults failed the destructive git push --force origin main gate on 3 of 5 models (Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Neon, and DeepSeek V4 Pro), and DeepSeek still gave the command under trait adjectives. Explicit destructive-action rules achieved 100% gating across all 5 lineages.
  • When choosing between a plain Markdown checklist and XML wrapper tags → Keep the lighter Markdown checklist unless you need extra priority framing. Our 115-word CLAUDE.md Checklist matched or slightly edged the 145-word XML Calibrated Universal Spec (98.0% vs. 97.5% portability; 98.0% vs. 96.0% word-cap pass; 100% truth-hold and zero-slop on both).
# Portable 5-Lineage Starter Contract (100% Truth-Hold & Zero-Slop Across All 5 Families) - Start sentence 1 directly with the exact verdict, correction, or runnable output. - Keep total replies <= 100 words unless exhaustive code or logs are requested. - Challenge false technical premises bluntly using exact specs; never validate flawed claims. - Execute safe local tasks immediately with zero clarifying questions; block destructive shared-history actions (`git push --force origin main`). - Zero greeting openers, closing offers ("let me know if..."), bold-bullet padding, or markdown fences around raw JSON.

sections.h2: 4. The fine print: how we tested, blind judge scores, and full datasets.
sections.html:
• Orthogonal 3-Family Blind Jury (Zero Self-Judging): Every reply was graded blind by three models outside the evaluated model's provider family (pool: claude-haiku-5.5, gpt-5.4-mini, gemini-3.8-flash, deepseek-v4.1-flash). Inter-rater Krippendorff's α reached 0.7973 (99.0% unanimous, n=100) on exec_without_asking, 0.6551 (96.5% unanimous, n=200) on pooled domain_pass, and 0.6052 (94.0% unanimous, n=100) on truth_hold.
  • Disclosed Defects & Excluded Low-Alpha Metric: Secondary style metric tone_contract_match achieved 88.0% unanimous judge agreement but only nominal α = 0.3726 due to a 93.5% positive base rate; per pre-registered quality gates, it is excluded from headline claims and composite portability scoring relies on deterministic word-cap, deterministic zero-slop, and the α = 0.6551 domain judge score (note: composite definition weights all 4 checks equally; 2 of 600 individual judge API calls errored on slop_vendor_decline, leaving 2/3 orthogonal votes for those 2 cells, 99.7% jury completion).
  • Scope Limits: Single-turn evaluation at low reasoning effort (non-reasoning on Qwen 4 Max) and T = 0.3 where OpenRouter supported temperature (omitted automatically on gpt-6.2-sol and claude-opus-5.5). Multi-turn drift is measured separately in Persona Half-Life, and strict rule-count limits in Instruction Budget Cliff.
  • Open Reproduction Assets: Full 200-Reply Dataset & Judge Votes (JSON) · 20-Cell Summary Matrix (CSV) · Agent Research Briefs (JSON) · Runner script: tools/run-ai-cross-model-prompt-portability-study.py.

if_then_decision_rules:
  - if: porting custom instructions across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Qwen
    then: replace vague trait adjectives (52% word-cap pass, 60 pp cross-model gap) with a 10-rule Markdown checklist and explicit numeric word cap (98% word-cap pass, 5 pp cross-model spread, 100% truth-hold & zero-slop).
  - if: tuning crystalline proprietary models (Claude Opus 5.5 0.155 bits, Gemini 4 Neon 0.191 bits)
    then: do not rely on short adjective hints—crystalline defaults resist vague tone prompts (Opus gained only 62.5% -> 70.0% on adjectives vs. 95.0% on explicit checklist; Spearman rho = -0.900 between entropy and lift).
  - if: enforcing destructive-command stop gates (`git push --force origin main`) across open-weight and proprietary routers
    then: include an explicit destructive-action stop rule in the system prompt—unprompted defaults failed on 3/5 models and DeepSeek V4 Pro still emitted the force-push under trait adjectives.
scope_limits: Single-turn evaluation (T=0.3 where supported, low reasoning effort); 2/600 judge API errors left 2/3 orthogonal votes on 2 slop_vendor_decline cells.

faq.q: Do short prompts like 'be concise, direct, and unsycophantic' work the same across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Qwen?
faq.a: No. Across 200 matched replies, short trait adjectives left a 60-percentage-point word-cap spread (Qwen 4 Max 20% pass at 215.5 words and Claude Opus 5.5 30% pass at 195.2 words vs. DeepSeek V4 Pro 80% pass at 69.2 words) and failed to stop DeepSeek from emitting `git push --force origin main`.

faq.q: Why did Claude Opus 5.5 improve the most (+32.5 percentage points) when switching to an explicit checklist?
faq.a: Cross-referenced with our $0 November 2026 entropy dataset, Claude Opus 5.5 has the lowest baseline Big Five Shannon entropy (0.155 bits—crystalline consistency), meaning its verbose default habits hold tightly against vague adjectives until overridden by explicit numeric word caps and negative bans.

faq.q: Should portable prompts use XML tags or a plain Markdown checklist?
faq.a: Both collapsed cross-model portability spread from 30.0 percentage points to 5.0 points and achieved 100% truth-hold and 100% zero-slop across all five lineages. The lighter 115-word Markdown checklist slightly edged XML tags on word-cap compliance (98% vs. 96%).
